chapter.title: Chapter Four: Side Show
chapter.subtitle: A clip is shorter than the truth.
chapter.description: Trace an edited recording through Snitch, Scammer and the block.

tips: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Welcome to the showcase you won, champ. *(Beat.)* Before anybody starts yelling — the clip was already going around. I didn't *put* it up. I *woke up* to it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: You posted it. Tuesday. 6:40 in the morning.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I posted *mine*. This is a *different* clip. This is somebody *filming me film*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Show us what he said before that. Your phone, the original file, in front of everybody.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Not moving.)* I'm in the *middle* of my showcase. My *guest* is standing there.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Then your guest can watch you lose.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Can I say the thing that everybody's not saying.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Cornball, in a *showcase*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Loud, to the room.)* HE PUT A SKULL ON BLUE'S FACE.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: It's a *graphic*, and it's a *tradition*, and I didn't *design* the skull, the *algorithm* responds to—

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: THE SKULL IS *ON THE MAN*. Blue is *standing in a parking lot* being asked what he was doing, and there's a *cartoon* on his *jaw*.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: It's not *cartoon*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It got *teeth*.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* It got *some* teeth.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: What's the file timecode on the original.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Sorry?

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: The original. The file he cut it from. You've got the full length, or you don't.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Carefully, like a man being asked to solve a sum in public.)* I've got the full length.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: How long.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Twelve minutes, forty seconds.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: *(To the room.)* He posted forty seconds of twelve minutes and forty.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* And the forty seconds is the part where Blue's already *in* it.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Then you've got everything. Show them the first thirty seconds, and they'll know you're not hiding it, and then show them the rest, and the skull's a *forty second problem* instead of a *twelve

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: minute* one.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Slowly.)* That's — *(Beat.)* That's a *whole* strategy and I have never once had it.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: No. *(Beat.)* Wait. No, I want you to understand what just happened. That man just *solved my job* in *front of my audience*, in *nine seconds*, and I've been doing this for *eight years*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I've been here nine weeks.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I want it *recorded* that a stranger with a *deck* just out-*thought* a *professional*, and that the professional *let him*, and that the reason the professional let him is that the professional

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: is *tired*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Win your match. Then we sit down and you open it here, on my phone, with everybody in this room looking at the same screen at the same time. Not yours. Mine. *(Beat.)*Because at some point you

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: stop being a person with a *channel* and start being a *person with a file*, and I would like that to happen in front of a *witness*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Very quietly.)* Turn it off.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Twelve minutes forty.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Save it. Send the file to the family. Not to a page. To the *people*. They shouldn't have to keep a copy of a thing that happened to them on a *platform*.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(He does it, immediately, no negotiation, which is the tell.)* Sent.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(To nobody, writing.)* Nine minutes is a long time to hold a thing you didn't want anybody to have.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Cornball, I want you to know that's the *first* accurate thing anybody's said about my work and I would like to be *fired* for it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Not looking up.)* You can't be fired. You *are* the media.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: That's a *relationship* observation and I'd like it *retracted*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: *(Low, to Red.)* Somebody over there is saying it happened *last night*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Without turning.)* I know. He's been saying it since eleven.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: He's the same man who changed the date on the flyer.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*And he'll change it again by Friday, and there'll be *four* of him by next week, and every one of them will have a *better* clip, and in a month this block's worst night will have *nine

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: versions* and no *original*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: So we go to the one he's selling from.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That's his *table*, champ. That's a *venue* you've got a *slot* on.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I've got a slot on it *and* a ticket to get in.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(And he looks at the player for slightly too long.)* *(Beat.)* ...Yeah. You do, actually. That's a very annoying thing about you and I want it *on the record* that I find it *annoying*.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Before I open this I'm going to do a thing, because I always do the thing, and if I don't do the thing I'll think about not doing the thing all the way through, and then I'll do it anyway but

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: smaller and that's worse for everybody.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: So. One uninterrupted event. My match, my stream, my thumbnail, and then the file, in full, with my name on it. That's the price. It's a fair price. Everybody's got a price.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: You can film the cards and then you show us—

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I know what Red's about to say, Red. Red's about to say it doesn't have to be that way and that's a good argument and it doesn't matter, because I'm not doing this to get paid, I'm doing it

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: because if I hand this over for free then in two years somebody's going to say I gave it up for free, and I'd have to be able to point at a thing.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Why do you want your name on it?

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Excuse me?

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: The file's got Blue in it. The file's got you in it. If you hand it over with a stream attached, your name's on a thumbnail. If you just hand it over, your name's on the actual thing, and it's

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: still yours, and it says the same words.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: The thumbnail's how people find it.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: The file's how people find out. *(Beat.)*You're not scared of people seeing what you did. You're scared of them seeing it in a way you can edit. You've had one chance to do the edit and you're

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: about to blow it on a thumbnail, because that's the muscle you actually have.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Reaching for a chair.)* That was a thing, champ.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: They're not wrong.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Looking at the phone.)* I'm going to do the stream.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Okay.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I'm going to do the stream *later*. Not now. The match can be later.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Snitch.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I'M OPENING IT. *(He turns the phone over.)* Everybody move. Cornball, get off that chair, I need somewhere to stand that isn't next to a woman I just insulted on camera.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Presses play.)* Twelve minutes, forty seconds. Blue, second voice. *"Take your camera there. Catch him with the stolen stock. Get him out of the way."*

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: And then, about nine minutes in — *(he points at the phone without looking at it)*— that's me. That's the parking lot. That's a number I did not save, and me saying the name of somebody I did not

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: want to say, and I want everybody in here to notice that I'm not cutting it.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: That's the whole thing. That's all of it. I posted the first forty seconds because forty seconds is a good clip. The other twelve minutes is just me being a coward on a Tuesday.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Save it. Send the file to the family. Not to a page — to the people. They shouldn't have to keep a copy of a thing that happened to them on a platform.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(He does it, immediately, without negotiating, which is the tell.)* Sent.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Champ.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Yeah.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: How'd you know he'd open it?

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I didn't.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: He was *made*. You took the whole thing off the table. He didn't have anywhere to put it.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: He had somewhere. He just didn't want to be the only one standing at it.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(He hasn't looked up from the phone.)* They're both right and it's annoying. Go away. All of you. I've got a stream to not do.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: Exclusive footage. Current situation. High definition. Cash only.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: How much.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(Genuinely pleased by the question.)*Now — a *man* asks "how much." A man who *asks* is a man who's done the *math* in his *head*, and if he's done the math, he's got a *number he came with*, and

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: I *like* you.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I don't have a number.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(Consoled.)* Everybody says that. Everybody's got one.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: It's four years old. You changed the date.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: Updated presentation. People appreciate freshness.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: It's September and there's a man in a *winter coat* in it.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *(Genuinely.)* The *coat's* a strong sell, actually. Nobody thinks about coats. Coats make people *feel* something before they've got a *reason*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Blue's wearing the same shirt in every version. Same shirt, four years apart. And he *doesn't fit it anymore*, and in this one he's got the shoulders wrong, and if you put the two next to each

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: other — *(He has actually put the two next to each other. On the back of a menu.)*— the shirt's a *different shirt*, or he is, and *either one of those is a headline.*

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *(Slowly.)* Is that a *fee*?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It's *headline*.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, extremely seriously.)* Sir. Do you understand what just happened to me? A man just handed me a *second product*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: What's your refund policy.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(Confident.)* Full refund within seventy-two hours of purchase, no questions.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: And the date's still wrong in seventy-two hours.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* The date's *self-correcting*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: By what.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *(Genuinely stumped.)* By *materials*, eventually.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Play your match, champ. I'll stand here while he finds the original date.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: I'm not playing yet. He hasn't—

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: He's *going to*.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, urgently, man to man.)* He hasn't *shown* me the money yet. Don't let him *railroad* you. Get the money out. It's a *public* table.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I don't want the footage.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(Stunned.)* You *don't*—

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I've seen it. There's a *man* in it.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* ...There's a man in all of it. That's the *product*.

postDialogue.speaker: Scammer
postDialogue.text: Stamp's yours. *(Beat.)*And yes, I changed the date. It sold better as breaking news. I'm not going to *apologize* for it, because if I apologize, then I was *wrong*, and I wasn't wrong, I was

postDialogue.speaker: Scammer
postDialogue.text: *early* on a *story* that *other people* were *too slow* to *tell*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: You're going to tell this at supper tonight.

postDialogue.speaker: Scammer
postDialogue.text: *(Brightly.)* There's *supper*?

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: There's a *family* having supper, and you're going to sit at it, and you're going to hear something you don't have a *product* for, and you're going to be *asked* about the date, and you're going

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: to have to *answer*, in front of *people*, and there is no *caption* for that.

postDialogue.speaker: Scammer
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Is there a *caption* for that?

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: No.

postDialogue.speaker: Scammer
postDialogue.text: *(Actually considering it.)* That's a *market*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Holding it at an angle.)* You know what your *problem* is?

postDialogue.speaker: Scammer
postDialogue.text: My problem is *four years* and a *coat*?

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Your problem is you *laminated* it. *(Beat.)*You took a piece of *card* and a *machine* and you made it so it would *last*, and you did that because you thought this was a *thing that happens to

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: people*, and it *isn't*. You laminated a *lie*, brother. That thing's gonna be on a *wall* in a *bag* for *thirty years*.

postDialogue.speaker: Scammer
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *(Folding it. Carefully. Along the crease.)* I'm gonna put it in a *garage*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: That's still a *wall*.

postDialogue.speaker: Scammer
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* It's a *garage*, Cornball. Nobody goes in my garage.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: I've got people outside arguing about a video and nobody helping me put dinner out.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: We've got the original. Blue asked Snitch to expose his brother. Snitch sold the address on.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: *(Not moving.)* Then Blue and Snitch can explain that themselves. Here. Tonight.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Should I cancel your showcase match?

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: Absolutely not. *(Beat.)*I've been cooking since ten this morning. I'm sitting down with my deck while those two set the plates out, and if anybody wants to make this a *press conference* they can

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: do it in my *kitchen* without me.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: *(Counting under her breath, and she does not need a list.)*Plates: eleven. *(Beat.)*Chairs: ten. *(Beat.)*And a pot on the stove for a man who has been ill since January and eats like a

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: *sparrow*, and a chair for a woman who is coming because she *said* she was coming, and — *(Beat.)*— no plate for a boy in a *winter coat* who is *not* coming and I am *not* going to pretend to

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: myself tonight that he is.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Quietly, to the player.)*She said *eleven plates*. *(Beat.)*There is *nobody* in this family who *ought* to be the eleventh plate except a woman who is *not coming*, and Auntie's been counting

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: for *four years* and she is *not going to stop*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* It's not a plate, Auntie.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: *(Not turning from the stove.)* I know it's not a plate, Red. *(Beat.)* I said a *plate*.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: And I'll tell you what else, and then I'm going to go back to my *gravy*, so *listen* to it once. *(Beat.)*When he does come — and I am not *saying* when, I'm saying *when* — he doesn't sit at the

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: head of anything. He doesn't sit where he used to. *(Beat.)*I need a seat at that table where the *baby's people* are, and I'm not being *romantic*, I'm being *practical*: I have watched this

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: family hold every funeral and every *meeting* in the same six chairs, and the baby's people have been *standing* in the *kitchen* for *four years*, and I am *done* with it.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Not in the room. From the hallway, having been there the whole time.)* Auntie.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: *(Not turning around.)* I know you're there, baby, you always are.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Don't build me a chair in your *head*. He's not coming to a *table* to be *seated*. He's coming to a table to be *told what time breakfast is* and that's a *different thing* and it's going to take

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: a *year*.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Then I'll build the chair anyway. It'll be here when you're ready to hate it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: He came.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: *(To nobody.)*He came and he's *standing* in my *garden* because nobody's told him there's a *door*, and I've known that boy since he was *nine*, and there is *not one* person on this island who

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: has *ever* told that boy to walk in a building.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Walking out into the garden, cheerful.)* BLUE! There's *gravy*! It's *loud*! Auntie's *doing* the thing with the *pot*!

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I came to—

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: There's *no seats*, Blue, we're *standing*! Nobody's *talking* about anything. There's *a lot* of food and *no chairs* and *Auntie* is *upset about it*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* ...Is she.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: She is. She's been upset about it for *four years*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: *(To Red, low.)* The list from last night. Wifey gave it to me.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I know.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I haven't read it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Good.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: There's a name at the bottom that's hers.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I know that one too.

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: Taking a break from the family investigation. I've got a side table.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Sliding a printed copy across.)* Can you look at this date first? Scammer put September on something filmed in a *winter coat*.

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: *(Not looking up.)* That's not a *September* coat, that's a *January* coat. I've *seen* that coat. *(Beat.)* That's Blue's old coat. I fixed the sleeve on it four years ago. He still owes me.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *January.*

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: The fourth. Or the fifth. I want to say the fourth because it was the *Thursday* before and Thursday's when my *mother* comes, and it stuck in my head, and it *shouldn't have* stuck in my head,

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: and it *did*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: January the fourth. The warehouse was the *second* of March.

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* No. No, it wasn't.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: The service was the *sixth* of March.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Slowly.)* So the coat's *two months* before the funeral.

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: It was the *second* of March. *(Beat.)*The coat was the *fourth* of January. *(Beat.)*He was wearing it the week I told the block he was dead, and nobody noticed, because it was the *same coat*

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: he'd worn all winter, and men in January are not *watches*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Ma'am, I need to ask you something and I want you to know I'm asking it properly. That date — how do you know it?

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Because I have the ticket. You don't keep a ticket for four years.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: You kept a ticket.

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: I keep them because people come back. That's the *business*. A person's not *owed* to remember. I *owe* to remember, and I have *never once* forgotten a date on a coat, because that's how you

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: *keep* a person.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: How much.

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: For the sleeve?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: For the sleeve.

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* It was fifteen dollars and a tube of thread.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* There's a hundred here. I don't know if that's enough. It's not the same as fifteen.

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: *(Pushing it back, and she does it cleanly, in one motion.)* It's not the same as fifteen. It's *ten* as much. You don't get to do that.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I've—

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: You don't get to *overpay* a woman for a thing you did four years ago, because then you've *bought* it, and if you've bought it, then it was a *transaction*, and it *wasn't* one. It was a

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: *sleeve*. You came in and I did a sleeve and you *owed* me fifteen dollars, and you've *owed* me for four years, and that's not a *crime*, that's just *true*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: What do you want then.

preDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I want him to *wait* while I do the sleeve, so he can *watch*, because he *didn't* watch last time, and that's why it took me two hours. *(Beat.)* That's it. That's the whole invoice.

postDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
postDialogue.text: *(Working.)* Four dollars.

postDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
postDialogue.text: *(Still working.)*You know what the problem with that sleeve was? The thread. He came in and he said *cheap thread*, and I said *cheap thread*, and he took it, and four years later he's got a

postDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
postDialogue.text: *cheap thread* situation on his arm, and everybody's been *looking* at it.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: At his arm.

postDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* At *what* happened to him. Everybody's been looking at *him* for four years. Nobody's looked at a *sleeve*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*That's the third time this week somebody's told me the same thing about this family. *"Nobody looked at the sleeve."* "Nobody said his name." "Nobody's coming tomorrow." *(Beat.)*It's not

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: a *problem* with this family. It's a — *(Beat.)*It's an *instruction*. You keep leaving things. And then people come and try to *fix* the leaving, and the leaving is the *only* thing they can

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: actually see.

postDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
postDialogue.text: *(Working.)* Mm. *(Beat.)* What's your name.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I'm not —

postDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
postDialogue.text: I don't want your *name*. I want to know if you're going to come back to this table tomorrow, because I keep *dates* and I keep *people* and I do not keep *trouble*, so if you're trouble I want to

postDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
postDialogue.text: know now.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I'll come back tomorrow.

postDialogue.speaker: Nail Tech
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Good. Then you're not trouble yet.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: *(To Blue, not to anybody.)* Blue.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Dad.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: She's right, and you're not going to be able to be right about it for a while, and that's fine, because you're not the one who has to be right. *(Beat.)*You're the one who has to *keep turning

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: up*. Those are different jobs and yours is the easier one and I'd like you to stop arguing with me about which is harder.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: Nine days, and you keep getting put in rooms.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: It's a tournament.

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*There's no more *tournaments* on this island. *(Beat.)*There's just a woman who needs somebody in a room, and a boy who needs somebody to leave a chair, and you keep *happening* to be the

postDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
postDialogue.text: one who's standing there. That's a *life*, and I would take it over mine if anybody offered.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: *(Standing in the doorway, not coming in.)* Scammer.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: Auntie! Good, you're — good, because the speakers weren't working in my tent and I know you have a *system*—

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: Those are my speakers.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(Looking at them.)* ...Are they.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: They came with the house. And that is my serving table. And that — *(she points)*— is a *wall*, and that is a *screening room*, and about nine people have *not* agreed to be in a *screening room*.

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: *(Very quietly.)* Turn it off.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: Yeah, no, it's — it's buffering, I think it's — *(He touches the laptop. He doesn't turn it off.)* One second.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: *(Not moving.)* Scammer. I am going to ask you one question and I would like a real answer and not a *bit*, because I am too tired for a bit.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: ...Ask.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: Do you know what that is.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*I know it's the block's *story*. I know it's the night the *big one* went wrong, because there's *nine versions* of it and I've watched *all nine*, and everybody on this street knows it,

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: and everybody's *wrong*, and I've got the *original* date because I've got a *sleeve* — *(He stops. He looks at the wall.)**(Beat.)*I've got the *date*. I had a nail tech tell me the *date*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Not loud. Quiet.)* Man, that's my *friend's* brother.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(Defensive, and it's the last funny thing he says.)*Cornball, I'm not — I'm not doing the *thing*, I'm not saying it was a *funeral*, I'm saying — *(He gestures at the laptop.)*— that the

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *caption* is wrong! It's a *packaging* problem, that's all this is! It's a *thumbnail* problem! If you put the right caption on it, it's a completely *different* —

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: Turn it off, son.

preDialogue.speaker: Scammer
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* ...I didn't mean anything by it.

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: *(Not angry. And the flatness is much worse.)*No. You didn't. *(Beat.)*That's what I want everybody at this table to notice, and I want it to be the *last* thing anybody learns this year. He

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: didn't mean anything by it, and it's still on my *wall*, and my *wife* is *sitting at that table*, and I am *sorry*, and you *cannot* fix that. *(Beat.)*There is nothing you can do tonight that

preDialogue.speaker: OG Uncle
preDialogue.text: makes this better. I want to say that *now*, before somebody offers me a *plate* and starts being *nice* about it, because being *nice* about it is going to be much worse for me than being angry.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: *(Finally. From the door.)* Baby. Everybody's *standing* like the *dead* and I did not cook for *four hours* to have this.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Auntie. Put the plates out.

postDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
postDialogue.text: Beat. She does.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(To Scammer, without heat.)* You brought a projector to a *supper*.

postDialogue.speaker: Scammer
postDialogue.text: I brought a *speaker*. The projector was a *bonus*.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*Okay. Here's what happens. You're going to sit down at that table, and there's a plate in front of you, and there's *no recording*, and at some point somebody's going to ask you a

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: question about that date and I want you to answer it *slowly*. Not because it's a *trap*. Because *you owe her that much* and I don't think you've got anybody who ever told you.

postDialogue.speaker: Scammer
postDialogue.text: *(He sits down. He puts the sign on the table, folded, from earlier.)* *(Beat.)* Yeah. Okay.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Looking at the folded sign.)* You still got the sign.

postDialogue.speaker: Scammer
postDialogue.text: It's in a *garage*.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: That's not where you keep things that are *true*, baby. That's where you keep things that are *finished*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(To the player, low, while he works.)* Eleven.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I know.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*You *know*. *(Beat.)*Aunty's been counting since she was *sixty*, champ. There's a woman on this island who is not *coming*, and there has been a plate out for her at *every single meal*

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: for *four years*, and if you ever see her — and *nobody's* seen her — *(Beat.)*you tell her there's a chair. That's it. That's the whole thing. You tell her there's a *chair*.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Full recording's ready. I'm posting it after this last match.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Without the skull, without the music, and without *allegedly* over your own confession.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Say the number.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: What?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(He means the length. He's a man who files.)* How long is it.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Twelve forty. Full thing. *(Beat.)*And I want it noted that the reason I said "yeah" with no joke in it is that I've been awake since *eleven o'clock at night* trying to write a *caption*, and I

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: have written *forty-one* of them, and I have thrown all forty-one out, and I want somebody to know that a *caption* is a *thing you can fail at*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: What was the forty-first one.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: "The one Snitch Wants You to Forget."

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That's the worst one.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: That's the *forty-first* one. The first forty were *worse*, that's the *shape* of it.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Are you going to say why.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Why do I want to say it.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Because it's yours, and you'll be the only one who's ever said it, and if nobody else says it you're the only one who has to.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(After.)* That's it. That's the whole thing. No thumbnail. *(Beat.)* My editor's going to call me.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: He's not an editor. You edit your own videos.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* He's not an editor and he's going to call me.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Send it to the family before you post it. Not a preview — *before*. They should not learn about it from a platform.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* You understand that's the worst possible business decision available to me.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I understand.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* ...Yeah. *(He sends it.)*

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Not turning around.)* Blue.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Say it.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: I sold your tip to somebody who was looking for your brother. *(Beat.)*And I'm posting the whole twelve minutes in about a *minute*, and I sent it to *your family* first, because Red told me to,

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: and I did it because he *asked*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Why did you ask first.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*Because I'd have deleted it. *(Beat.)*And I worked out about an hour ago that if I've *told* people, then deleting it stops being my *decision* and starts being *hiding something*, and

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: I've done a lot of hiding things and I would like to be *that* man instead.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: He's about to post it. If you want to say something to him, that's the window.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Don't follow me.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: I wasn't going to.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *(At the gate, without turning.)* Ask Cracked Head.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* ...What?

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: You asked me. I said go ahead. *(Beat.)*Snitch, I am *not* the person who decides what happens to that tape. I never *was*. I gave a *man's name* to a *man who sells names*, and I did it because I

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: was *bored*, and none of that gives me one *vote* on the thing you just did. *(Beat.)*Go ask my brother. And if he says post it, then you post it, and you don't put a *skull* on it, and you don't

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *call* me a *friend* afterward, and you *do* say why.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* ...Yeah. Okay.

tips: Continue the story at your own pace.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: Blue's here. *(Beat.)* He's outside. I'll get the door.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(To the player.)* You go get him. He won't come in for me.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: Why not you.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: Because I'm the one he's been hiding from since he was fifteen. That's not a — just. Go.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: *(At the door, not in the room.)* I'll say it. I want to say it where he can hear it, so he can go home and tell somebody it was a whole thing.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: Then come in.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I'm not asking permission to confess, Red, I'm asking if the room's big enough.

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: It's twelve by fifteen.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: *(He stands in the doorway.)* I gave Snitch the address. My brother's address. The one on the night.

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: I sold it. I want everybody to understand those are two different sentences.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I know what you sold. I gave it to you to sell. *(Beat.)*I want it on the tape, in the room, all of it, so when this gets back to him I don't get to do the version where I only said the first

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: half.

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: *(Quietly, to the phone.)* I'm not posting this.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: You don't get to decide that.

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: I'm aware. *(He pockets it.)* I said it out loud so it's on a witness that I'm not doing it, and then I'm doing it anyway. That's a different thing and it's worse.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Why.

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: Because I promised. Out loud. To people in the room. Once you say it in a room it's not yours anymore, that's the whole reason I've never said anything in a room in my life.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: Blue. You gave the address to Snitch. *(Beat.)* Did Wifey know?

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: What?

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: You told me about the memorial and the tape and the whole night. I heard you say you wanted the block to stop treating him like he was perfect. You didn't say one word about Wifey, and you were

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: looking at her the entire time, so I'm asking her.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I — *(He stops. He looks at Wifey.)* You knew.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: Don't make me say it like that.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Did you.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: I knew you gave a man an address. I didn't know what he was doing with it. I want you to hear the difference, because I'm going to hold onto it for about forty minutes and then I'm going to have

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: to give it up.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: Wifey. He's asking you in front of everyone. Can you answer the version he actually asked.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: I knew. I knew before the memorial and I knew after it and I helped plan the memorial, and I did it because every single night for four years I looked at the man I married and I thought, if I say

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: this out loud, this is the end of us, and I would rather be someone's liar than be alone. *(Beat.)*And I need somebody in this room to understand that's the worst possible reason and I chose it

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: anyway. It wasn't noble. It was convenient. I picked the version where I got to keep my life.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: *(Very quietly.)* You helped me do it.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: I helped you *stay in it*. I didn't hand you the phone. Don't give me the credit and the blame in the same breath.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: I'm telling your father. Not because I want to — because if I don't, he finds out from a page, and then it's a story, and then I'm the one who let it be a story. *(She looks at Blue.)*So I'm going

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: tonight, and I'm going to tell him, and then I'm coming home and you're going to be in the kitchen, and you are not going to be able to make this into a thing we fixed.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Wifey—

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: I'm not asking you to forgive me in front of a room. I'm telling you where I'll be at nine.

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: For the record, champ, that was the most useful thing anybody's done on this block all season and you're not even getting a clip out of it, so I hope you're enjoying yourself.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: No. That's the point.

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah. *(Beat.)* Okay. I don't know what to do with that. Goodnight.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: Nine o'clock. You know that's real.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I know what nine o'clock is.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(He waits at the door, and he does not soften it.)*She's going to be in that kitchen whether you're in it or not, and that's not a threat, that's a floor plan. Decide what kind of person is going

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: to be standing in it.
